cause: Natural bitmap pixels were treated as CSS pixels, so OS display scaling and window zoom enlarged default 100 percent images. The reported PNG is 894x1341, without a density chunk; Markdown has no explicit width/zoom and saved settings are natural/100.
implementation: Use naturalWidth/devicePixelRatio for ordinary raster 100 percent, capped by the containing content box. Shared controls use the same baseline. Re-arm the resolution listener on density change and dispose it with its owner. Vector/srcset and explicit zoom retain their owners.
upstream: docs/vscode_design_sources.json#reading_image_density_20261025; bitmap pixel mapping is a product adaptation.

ui.scope: Real Chromium emulated density and page zoom; 64/894/3840px PNG, narrow content, SVG/srcset, dynamic source, Shadow reader, manual scale and Fit Width, source protection and disposal. Existing alignment/keyboard/anchor/theme and 20/100/1000 lifecycle regression retained.

native.scope: Original host private desktop, actual reported PNG copy, light/dark toolbar, trusted typing and ten fixed-position clicks, alignment undo/redo/save/reopen, authored zoom and unchanged source.

validation_notes: Old implementation reproduced extra enlargement at real Chromium DPR 1.20000005; red case 068b338784294dac954f4c677002f802 retained.

Initial native assertion included transparent image borders in bitmap pixels; corrected measurement subtracts the border. The second run reached existing authored zoom and refused navigation with unsaved changes; fixture now saves that temporary document before loading the reported image. Product guard preserved.
First local uninstall preflight command used a nonexistent script subdirectory and made no changes; corrected public root entry passed.
limits: No physical cross-monitor move, other-platform acceptance or full UI suite.

Full-screen and standalone image viewers retain their separate existing sizing.
User windows require normal restart; no window closure or live replacement.
Existing navigation/rendering/PPT and shell ownership issues remain open; no push authorized.
